name: Colorectal cancer
theme: the ctDNA frontier · organ preservation earned

meta.title: Colorectal cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults with colorectal adenocarcinoma - one spec for both primary sites, because staging, the universal MMR test, the adjuvant logic, and the entire metastatic ticket rack are shared verbatim; only the locoregional rectal limb (total neoadjuvant therapy and the organ-preservation question) diverges, and it lives here as a dedicated branch. The two forks that decide everything arrive early: WHERE (colon vs rectum - the radiation-and-organ-preservation question) and WHETHER MMR IS DEFICIENT (the immunoablation fork that now spans both sites). Anal squamous cancer and appendiceal tumors are different diseases with their own rows - rerouted, not absorbed. The registry's ctDNA frontier lives here: the first disease where a blood test has randomized evidence for guiding LESS chemotherapy (DYNAMIC), a stark prognostic split (GALAXY), and an honest negative for acting on it with more chemotherapy (ALTAIR) - prognostic is not yet actionable, and this trainer teaches the difference.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the registry's ctDNA frontier and its organ-preservation earners. Localized colon carries the double de-escalation: duration (IDEA - 3 months CAPOX suffices for low-risk stage III) and selection (DYNAMIC - ctDNA-guided stage II treatment halved chemotherapy use with 5-year RFS and OS intact, now mature in Nat Med 2025). Post-op ctDNA is the checkpoint: GALAXY's HR ~12 prognostic split renders honestly NEXT TO ALTAIR's failed intervention trial (FTD/TPI on molecular recurrence: DFS HR 0.79, p=0.107 - NOT met) - the biomarker is real, acting on it with m…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: AJCC 8th edition TNM (v9 colorectal chapter status unconfirmed - flagged); universal MMR/MSI testing on every new diagnosis; RAS/BRAF/HER2 on all metastatic disease; sidedness recorded as biology
meta.response: RECIST 1.1 for metastatic disease; for rectal organ preservation the load-bearing read is clinical complete response (cCR) on the watch-and-wait pathway - a response category that IS the treatment decision

Newly diagnosed.name: Resection alone (stage I - surgery cures most)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: an operation and its recovery - then done; the lightest curative card in this trainer
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the earliest stage: an operation removes the cancer and cures most people - no chemotherapy needed afterward.
drugs: Segmental colectomy / proctectomy (or endoscopic resection, select T1)

Newly diagnosed.name: ctDNA-guided adjuvant decision (DYNAMIC - the selection de-escalation)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: randomized evidence for stage II selection (DYNAMIC); guideline uptake evolving (secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: for most (the ctDNA-negative), the toxicity is what this strategy REMOVES: no chemotherapy at all
Newly diagnosed.patient: After surgery for stage II colon cancer: a blood test can decide whether chemotherapy is needed at all - in the trial, half as many people got chemo, and five years later the cure rates were the same.
drugs: Tumor-informed ctDNA assay routing adjuvant chemotherapy

Newly diagnosed.name: Risk-adapted adjuvant chemotherapy (IDEA - the duration de-escalation)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN category 1 adjuvant framework (secondhand); IDEA duration logic embedded in guidelines
Newly diagnosed.evidence: pooled analysis of 6 RCTs (IDEA, NEJM 2018) - the duration evidence; the 5-yr OS figure itself is a flagged teaching estimate
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: oxaliplatin neuropathy is the tax the IDEA came to cut: three months instead of six halves the cumulative dose for the low-risk majority
Newly diagnosed.patient: After surgery for higher-risk disease: a chemotherapy course lowers the chance of return - and a 12,000-patient study showed many people need only half as long a course as before.
drugs: CAPOX or FOLFOX, duration by risk (3 vs 6 months)

Newly diagnosed.name: Total neoadjuvant therapy +/- organ preservation (PRODIGE-23 / OPRA)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: TNT 'currently the preferred approach for most patients' - NCI PDQ's own language (loaded live); NCCN rectal v2026 secondhand
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (PRODIGE-23, RAPIDO) + randomized organ-preservation strategy (OPRA)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the longest curative road in this trainer: months of chemo, then radiation, then surgery or the surveillance commitment - the organ-preservation fork trades an…
Newly diagnosed.patient: For rectal cancer that has grown locally: all the medicine first (chemo, then radiation), then surgery - except that people whose cancer disappears completely on treatment can sometimes keep the rectum and be watched closely instead, with the same survival.
drugs: Induction FOLFIRINOX/CAPOX -> chemoradiation -> TME or watch-and-wait

Newly diagnosed.name: dMMR immunoablation (Cercek dostarlimab NOM / NICHE-2 - the card that refuses to rank)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: guideline placement evolving (secondhand); AZUR trials are the randomized confirmations in flight
Newly diagnosed.evidence: single-arm phase 2 (NEJM 2022 + expanded NEJM 2025; NICHE-2 NEJM 2024) - young, spectacular, labeled
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: checkpoint-inhibitor immune ledger - and for the rectal cohort, the absence of every other toxicity: no radiation, no operation, no chemotherapy
Newly diagnosed.patient: If the tumor's DNA-repair test is deficient: immune treatment alone has made every rectal tumor in the key study disappear completely - so far without surgery or radiation for any of those patients. It is early, single-study evidence, and this card says so as loudly as it says the result.

Newly diagnosed.name: Sidedness-aware chemotherapy backbone (1L stage IV, no ticket)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN 1L framework (secondhand); sidedness-directed antibody choice on pooled randomized evidence
Newly diagnosed.evidence: randomized programs (pooled sidedness analysis verified); the median itself flagged pending PARADIGM PMID resolution
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: cumulative chemotherapy ledger (neuropathy, fatigue) plus the chosen antibody's signature (rash for EGFR, pressure/protein for bev)
Newly diagnosed.patient: For spread disease without a special test-result door: chemotherapy plus an antibody - which antibody depends, genuinely, on which side of the colon the cancer started.
drugs: Doublet chemotherapy + bevacizumab or anti-EGFR by sidedness

Newly diagnosed.name: Checkpoint blockade first-line (MSI-H stage IV - KEYNOTE-177 / CheckMate 8HW)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: checkpoint-first for MSI-H mCRC (guideline placement secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 - PFS decisively met in both; OS honesty carried verbatim
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the immune ledger (colitis chief among them for the doublet) - traded against indefinite chemotherapy, which most of these patients never need
Newly diagnosed.patient: If the spread cancer's DNA-repair test is deficient: immune treatment beats chemotherapy decisively and lasts for years in many - the strongest first choice in this situation, shown here with its young-numbers label because the longest-term counts are still being written.

Newly diagnosed.name: Encorafenib + cetuximab + chemo (BRAF V600E 1L - BREAKWATER)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: FDA accelerated approval incl. 1L (recorded in the NEJM primary; date secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS met, interim OS HR 0.49 (NEJM 2025)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: BRAF-inhibitor skin and joint signatures atop chemotherapy - a fuller schedule bought with a doubled median
Newly diagnosed.patient: If the tumor carries the BRAF mutation: a three-part combination doubled the middle survival time compared with chemotherapy alone - the biggest turnaround story on this menu.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; obstruction and bleeding management are the craft here
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining cancer-directed treatment is a real choice, made with real numbers - and with a team whose whole job is comfort.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: FTD/TPI + bevacizumab (SUNLIGHT - the ranked refractory standard)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: cytopenias are the tablet's tax; the antibody adds its pressure-and-protein watch
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: When earlier treatments stop working: a tablet-plus-antibody pair added three months to the middle survival time over the tablet alone - the best-proven option at this stage.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Fruquintinib (FRESCO-2 - the later door)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: hypertension and hand-foot skin reaction - the oral-TKI signature
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A once-daily tablet proven to extend survival after the standard options - a real, modest, honestly-sized benefit.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Sotorasib + panitumumab (KRAS G12C - CodeBreaK 300)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS met; OS underpowered/NS (carried verbatim)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the anti-EGFR rash plus TKI gut effects - visible and managed, not silent
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If the tumor carries the specific KRAS G12C change: a targeted pair more than doubled the time the cancer stayed controlled - though a survival advantage has not been formally shown, and the card says so.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Tucatinib + trastuzumab (HER2-amplified - MOUNTAINEER; T-DXd behind it)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: diarrhea (tucatinib) managed early; T-DXd carries the lung-inflammation watch (8%) named out loud
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If the tumor is HER2-positive: a chemotherapy-free targeted pair shrinks the cancer in about four in ten people - provisional-approval evidence, labeled as such, with a stronger drug waiting behind it.
drugs: Tucatinib + trastuzumab (T-DXd as the next card)

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: teaching estimate (flagged); randomized placebo-arm bracket verified
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort after several treatment lines is a real road, chosen with the true numbers on the table.

refs.label: NCI PDQ: Colon Cancer Treatment (HP, updated 2025-02-12, loaded live 2026-08) - stage-by-stage framework; explicitly separate from the rectal PDQ ('different therapeutic approaches, particularly regarding radiation')
NCI PDQ: Rectal Cancer Treatment (HP, updated 2025-02-12, loaded live 2026-08) - TNT 'currently the preferred approach for most patients' in PDQ's own words; watch-and-wait/NOM covered
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines: Colon Cancer and Rectal Cancer, current versions (nccn.org 403 - SECONDHAND, confirm versions and patient-guideline IDs on-site)

Grothey et al. IDEA collaboration: 3 vs 6 months adjuvant FOLFOX/CAPOX, 12,834 pts pooled from 6 RCTs - overall noninferiority NOT confirmed (DFS HR 1.07, CI 1.00-1.15, margin 1.12); CAPOX 3-mo noninferior (HR 0.95); low-risk T1-3N1 3-yr DFS 83.1 vs 83.3; T4/N2 favors 6 months. The duration answer, risk-stratified. NEJM 2018;378:1177-88 (PMID 29590544, verified)

Tie et al. DYNAMIC: ctDNA-guided adjuvant management in stage II colon - chemo use 15% vs 28%, 2-yr RFS 93.5% vs 92.4% (noninferior, margin -8.5pp). The selection de-escalation, randomized. NEJM 2022;386:2261-72 (PMID 35657320, verified)

Tie et al. DYNAMIC 5-year update: 5-yr RFS 88% vs 87%, 5-yr OS 93.8% vs 93.3% (HR 1.05) - mature; EOT ctDNA clearance highly prognostic (97% vs 0% 5-yr recurrence-free). Nat Med 2025 (PMID 40055522, verified)

Kotani/Nakamura et al. CIRCULATE-Japan GALAXY: post-op ctDNA positivity - DFS HR 11.99, OS HR 9.68 (n=2,240 update, Nat Med 2024, PMID 39284954); sustained clearance 24-mo DFS 89.0% vs 3.3%; primary Nat Med 2023 (PMID 36646802). The prognostic verdict, verified twice

ALTAIR (NCT04457297): trifluridine/tipiracil vs placebo in post-adjuvant ctDNA-positive, radiologically-NED CRC - median DFS 9.30 vs 5.55 months, HR 0.79, p=0.107 - primary endpoint NOT MET. The honest negative: prognostic is not yet actionable-for-escalation. Nat Med 2026 (PMID 42260101, verified)

Chalabi et al. NICHE-2: neoadjuvant nivolumab + ipilimumab in dMMR locally advanced colon cancer (n=115) - pathological response 98%, pCR 68%, no recurrences at median 26 months. NEJM 2024;390:1949-58 (PMID 38838311, verified; NCT03026140)

Cercek et al. PD-1 blockade in mismatch repair-deficient locally advanced rectal cancer: dostarlimab - 12/12 (100%) clinical complete response, no chemoradiation or surgery needed. NEJM 2022;386:2363-76 (PMID 35660797, verified; NCT04165772)

Cercek et al. Nonoperative management of mismatch repair-deficient tumors (expanded cohort, n=117): rectal 49/49 (100%) cCR - ALL nonoperative; non-rectal dMMR 35/54 cCR; 2-yr RFS 92%. FDA status in this setting NOT asserted - confirm via registry. NEJM 2025 (PMID 40293177, verified)

Conroy et al. PRODIGE-23: neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX then CRT then TME in locally advanced rectal cancer - 3-yr DFS 76% vs 69% (HR 0.69, p=0.034). Lancet Oncol 2021;22:702-15 (PMID 33862000, verified; NCT01804790)

Pooled analysis of triplet-induction TNT: 5-yr OS 86.8% - the maturity anchor behind the TNT card's 5-year figure. Cancer Treat Rev 2024 (PMID 39305700, verified; PRODIGE-23 7-yr update itself: confirm via registry)

Bahadoer et al. RAPIDO: short-course RT then chemotherapy then TME - 3-yr disease-related treatment failure 23.7% vs 30.4% (HR 0.75, p=0.019). CAVEAT CARRIED: later reports of higher locoregional failure in the experimental arm - confirm via registry. Lancet Oncol 2021;22:29-42 (PMID 33301740, verified; NCT01558921)

Garcia-Aguilar et al. OPRA: TNT with selective watch-and-wait - 3-yr DFS 76% both arms; 3-yr TME-free survival 41% (induction-first) vs 53% (CRT-then-consolidation) - about half preserve the organ without survival detriment. JCO 2022;40:2546-56 (PMID 35483010, verified; 5-yr update: confirm via registry)
Andre et al. KEYNOTE-177: pembrolizumab vs chemotherapy, 1L MSI-H mCRC - PFS 16.5 vs 8.2 months (HR 0.60). NEJM 2020;383:2207-18 (PMID 33264544, verified)

Diaz et al. KEYNOTE-177 final analysis: OS HR 0.74 (CI 0.53-1.03) - formal superiority NOT met at the split alpha, with 60% crossover; PFS HR 0.59. The crossover-honest OS, carried verbatim. Lancet Oncol 2022;23:659-70 (PMID 35427471, verified)

Andre et al. CheckMate 8HW: 1L nivolumab + ipilimumab vs chemotherapy, MSI-H mCRC - 24-mo PFS 72% vs 14% (p<0.001; HR 0.21 carried as reported pending full-text check). NEJM 2024;391:2014-26 (PMID 39602630, verified)

Andre et al. CheckMate 8HW nivo+ipi vs nivo monotherapy: PFS HR 0.62 (p=0.0003), median NR vs 39.3 months - the doublet question answered. FDA 1L status: confirm via registry. Lancet 2025;405:383-95 (PMID 39874977, verified)

Kopetz et al. BREAKWATER (1L BRAF V600E): encorafenib + cetuximab + mFOLFOX6 - PFS 12.8 vs 7.1 (HR 0.53); interim OS 30.3 vs 15.1 months (HR 0.49); the NEJM abstract itself records the accelerated FDA approval incl. first line (date secondhand). NEJM 2025 (PMID 40444708, verified; NCT04607421)
BREAKWATER response analysis: ORR 60.9% vs 40.0% - the accelerated-approval basis. Nat Med 2025 (PMID 39863775, verified)

Kopetz et al. BEACON (2L+ BRAF V600E): triplet OS 9.0 vs 5.4 (HR 0.52), doublet 8.4 (HR 0.60) - the old bar BREAKWATER doubled. NEJM 2019;381:1632-43 (PMID 31566309, verified; the oft-quoted 9.3/5.9 is the updated analysis - PMID unresolved, not cited)
Strickler et al. MOUNTAINEER: tucatinib + trastuzumab, HER2+ RAS-WT mCRC (2L+) - ORR 38.1%; accelerated approval (date secondhand). Lancet Oncol 2023;24:496-508 (PMID 37142372, verified; NCT03043313)
Raghav et al. DESTINY-CRC02: trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg - ORR 37.8%; ILD 8% (the named watch). Lancet Oncol 2024;25:1147-62 (PMID 39116902, verified; NCT04744831)
Yaeger et al. KRYSTAL-1: adagrasib + cetuximab, G12C mCRC - ORR 46%, PFS 6.9 months (mono 19%/5.6). NEJM 2023;388:44-54 (PMID 36546659, verified)
Fakih et al. CodeBreaK 300: sotorasib 960 + panitumumab vs standard care, chemorefractory G12C - PFS 5.6 vs 2.2 (HR 0.49). NEJM 2023;389:2125-39 (PMID 37870968, verified)
CodeBreaK 300 OS update: HR 0.70, NOT significant (underpowered, crossover); ORR 30.2% - the caveat carried verbatim on the card. JCO 2025 (PMID 40215429, verified)
Prager et al. SUNLIGHT: FTD/TPI + bevacizumab vs FTD/TPI - OS 10.8 vs 7.5 months (HR 0.61), PFS 5.6 vs 2.4. The ranked refractory standard. NEJM 2023;388:1657-67 (PMID 37133585, verified)
Dasari et al. FRESCO-2: fruquintinib vs placebo, refractory mCRC - OS 7.4 vs 4.8 (HR 0.66); FDA 2023-11 (secondhand). Lancet 2023;402:41-53 (PMID 37331369, verified)

Pooled analysis: primary tumour sidedness as driver of treatment choice in RAS-WT mCRC - anti-EGFR earns the left, bevacizumab holds the right. Eur J Cancer 2023 (PMID 36913832, verified). PARADIGM primary publication: PMID UNRESOLVED this sweep - deliberately not cited; TRIBE2 candidate PMID caught as a wrong-PMID trap (polymer-chemistry paper) - also not cited

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

CIRCULATE-US / NRG-GI008 (NCT05174169): ctDNA-guided adjuvant escalation/de-escalation, stage IIB-III colon, pMMR, n=1,912, phase 2/3, 915 US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08. BESPOKE (NCT04264702) is observational with UNKNOWN status - not listed

AZUR-2 (NCT05855200): perioperative dostarlimab vs SOC, dMMR/MSI-H resectable T4N0/stage III colon, n=892, phase 3, EFS primary, 27 US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08. AZUR-1 (rectal sibling, NCT05723562): ACTIVE NOT RECRUITING - named, not listed

MSK induction PD-1 blockade (NCT04165772, Cercek PI): dMMR locally advanced rectal (+ other dMMR solid tumors), phase 2, pCR/cCR-at-12-months primary, 10 US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08. JANUS (NCT05610163, pMMR TNT-triplet rectal): ACTIVE NOT RECRUITING - named, not listed; no broad-US pMMR rectal NOM randomized door verified open this sweep
CodeBreaK 301 (NCT06252649): sotorasib + panitumumab + FOLFIRI vs FOLFIRI+/-bev, 1L G12C mCRC, n=450, phase 3, PFS primary, 13 US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08
MOUNTAINEER-03 (NCT05253651): tucatinib + trastuzumab + mFOLFOX6 vs SOC, 1L HER2+ RAS-WT mCRC, n=400, phase 3, BICR-PFS primary, 108 US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08

PROCEADE-CRC-03 (NCT07549412): precemtabart tocentecan (anti-CEACAM5 ADC) +/- bev vs FTD/TPI + bev, refractory mCRC (<=2 prior metastatic regimens), n=1,020, phase 3 3-arm, OS primary, 18 US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08
